'''Donald Herman Voet''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|v|oʊ|t}} {{respell|VOHT}}; November 29, 1938 – April 11, 2023) was an American biochemist who was emeritus associate professor of chemistry at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. His laboratory used [[x-ray crystallography]] to understand structure-function relationships in proteins.<ref name="PennChem">{{cite web|url=https://www.chem.upenn.edu/profile/donald-voet|title=U. Penn, Dept. of Chemistry: Faculty Donald Voet|year=2013|publisher=University of Pennsylvania|access-date=22 Aug 2013}}</ref> He and his wife, [[Judith G. Voet]], are authors of biochemistry text books that are widely used in undergraduate and graduate curricula.<ref name="whatislife">{{cite web|url=http://www.whatislife.com/reviews/voet.htm|title=Reviews of books by Donald Voet, Judith Voet|last=Buehler |first=Lukas K. |date=January 2, 2000|publisher=Lukas K. Buehler |access-date=18 January 2010}}</ref><ref name="TiBS">{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/S0968-0004(99)01447-4|last=Wood|first= E.J.|date=1 October 1999|title=Book review: Biochemistry in a nutshell - Fundamentals of Biochemistry by Donald Voet, Judith G. Voet and Charlotte W. Pratt|journal=Trends in Biochemical Sciences|volume=24|issue=10|pages= 409–410}}</ref><ref name="IBB">{{cite journal|last=Sodja|first=Ann |year=1996|title=Book Review - Biochemistry|journal=International Biodeterioration & Biodegradation|volume=37|issue=3–4|pages=233–235|doi=10.1016/0964-8305(96)88252-7}}</ref><ref name="PDB">{{cite journal|date=Summer 2008|title=Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Education (BAMBED), a Journal for University, College, and High School Educators by Judith G. Voet1 and Donald H. Voet2, BAMBED Co-Editors-in-Chief|journal=Protein Databank Newsletter|publisher=RCSB PDB|issue=38|pages=5|url=http://ftp.wwpdb.org/pub/pdb/doc/newsletters/rcsb_pdb/news38_jul08.pdf}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Voet was born on November 29, 1938.<ref>{{Cite book | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=-BBYAAAAMAAJ&q=Donald+Voet+1938 | title = Teaching chemistry to students with disabilities: A manual for high schools, colleges, and graduate programs | isbn = 978-0-8412-3817-6 | last1 = Milner | first1 = Dorothy L | last2 = Committee On Chemists With Disabilities | first2 = American Chemical Society | year = 2001| publisher = American Chemical Society. }}</ref> He earned his B.S. in chemistry from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1960 and his Ph.D. in chemistry from [[Harvard University]] with [[William Lipscomb|William N. Lipscomb, Jr.]] in 1967.<ref name="PDB" /><ref name=Voet1964WNL/><ref name=Voet1967WNL/>

==Career==
Voet completed his postdoctoral research at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1969 in the laboratory of [[Alexander Rich]]. He later became a professor in the chemistry department at the University of Pennsylvania. Voet and his wife were coeditors-in-chief of the journal ''Biochemical and Molecular Biology Education''.<ref name="PennChem" /><ref name="PDB" />

==Death==
Voet died on April 11, 2023, at the age of 84.<ref>{{cite web |title=Donald Herman Voet (1938 – 2023) |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/donald-herman-voet-1938-2023/ |website=Chemistry Views |date=18 April 2023 |access-date=19 April 2023}}</ref>

==Notable publications==
*Voet, D; Voet, J.G.; and Pratt, C.W., ''Fundamentals of Biochemistry, Life at the molecular level'' (4th ed.), John Wiley & Sons (2013)
*Voet, D. and Voet, J, G., ''Biochemistry'' (4th ed.), John Wiley & Sons Inc.: Hoboken, NJ (2011)
*Voet, D; Voet, J.G.; and Pratt, C.W., ''Fundamentals of Biochemistry'' (3rd ed.), John Wiley & Sons (2008)
*Uzman, A.; Eichberg, J.; Widger, W.; Cornely, K.; Voet, D.; Voet, J.G.; and Pratt, C.W.; ''Student Companion to Accompany Fundamentals of Biochemistry'' (2nd ed.), John Wiley & Sons (2006)
*Voet, D; Voet, J.G.; and Pratt, C.W.; ''Fundamentals of Biochemistry'' (2nd ed.), John Wiley & Sons (2006)
*Voet, D. and Voet, J. G., ''Solutions Manual to Accompany Biochemistry'' (3rd ed.), John Wiley & Sons (2004)
*Voet, D. and Voet, J. G., ''Biochemistry'' (3rd ed.), John Wiley & Sons (2004)<ref name="PennChem" /><ref name="TiBS" />
